page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.8-32 is a flexible virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz, supported by 32 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Architectural CPU features include AVX, AES-NI, and SHA extensions, alongside 16 MB of L3 cache. No local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data, and no discrete GPUs are present.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily within the average performance tier across multi-threaded computational workloads. The system achieves a PassMark CPU score of 19,755.42 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,867.0. Single-core throughput is constrained, reflected in a stress-ng single-core score of 788.69 in the lower tenth percentile, while multi-core stress-ng reaches an average 6,302.32. Memory subsystem efficiency represents a relative strength, with PassMark memory scoring in the top quartile at 2,813.5 and uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 71.33 GB/sec.

From an efficiency standpoint, the VM.Standard.E3.Flex.8-32 provides balanced compute density for parallel tasks that do not demand cutting-edge per-thread clocks or advanced vector extensions like AVX-512. The 1:2 compute-to-memory configuration delivers cost-effective execution for scale-out applications, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and static web serving, where static throughput reached 15.51 GB/sec and Redis operations sustained 14.36 million operations per second.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.8-32 is a compute-focused flexible virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs) at 2.25 GHz coupled with 32 GB of RAM, offering a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no local storage or hardware accelerators, relying on remote block storage and dedicated CPU compute. Benchmark metrics show reliable multi-threaded throughput, registering 19,755.42 on PassMark CPU and 8,867.0 on Geekbench multi-core, complemented by upper-quartile PassMark memory performance. While single-thread execution is modest, multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth handle concurrent processing effectively. The platform is well matched for distributed workloads, build automation, web serving, and backend services.
